sections.overview: Nomada succincta is a European cuckoo bee whose best-supported hosts are Andrena nitida and A. nigroaenea.
sections.identification: Its common English name refers to yellow legs, but similar Nomada can be confused; a French field account distinguishes it from N. goodeniana by its more fully yellow tibiae and tarsi.
sections.habitat: Regional accounts record it in varied places, including railway land, dikes, woodland edges and heath; no single habitat is established for the full range.
sections.diet: As a cleptoparasite, its larvae use the host nest provisions rather than pollen collected by the female; adults may visit flowers for nectar.
sections.behavior: European accounts most often name A. nitida and A. nigroaenea as hosts; some list other Andrena as possible hosts, so those additional records remain provisional.
sections.reproduction: A Slovenian account describes one generation per year, with adults from April to June; local dates may vary with climate and host activity.
sections.ecology: It overlaps in season with other spring Nomada but has different documented hosts from N. leucophthalma, whose hosts are A. clarkella and A. apicata.
sections.conservation: The European Red List classifies N. succincta as Least Concern at European and EU scales; this does not imply it is common at every site.
